title: Token surge thresholds + regional prewarm heuristics (hosted API)
content:
SUMMARY:
This sheet captures a recommended set of surge thresholds (tokens/sec and QPS) and region-specific prewarm heuristics for the Hosted API. Purpose: give SRE/Capacity teams deterministic triggers to prewarm GPU slices and reserve headroom for short-duration token bursts without manual intervention.

SCOPE & HORIZON:
- Services: public hosted text generation endpoints (chat + completions) only.
- Time window: next 12 months (rolling forecasts used by capacity ops).
- Models in scope: medium/large family mix used in production as of Jan 2026 (see assumptions).

KEY ASSUMPTIONS (baseline):
- Avg tokens/request: 60 tokens for standard completions, 220 tokens for chat sessions (weighted mix below).
- Model mix (baseline): 55% medium-class (lower-cost), 40% large-class (higher latency/cost), 5% embedding/rerank.
- Effective tokens/sec per GPU-slice: 22,000 tokens/sec (A100-80-equivalent slice, KV-cache active, mixed model assumptions).
- Desired SLA: P99 latency < 350ms for short-completion traffic; tail-latency buffer used to size prewarm windows.
- Safety multiplier for spot/eviction-prone regions: +15% headroom.

REGIONAL PROJECTIONS AND RECOMMENDED HEADROOMS (snapshot baseline):
| region      | proj_peak_tokens_per_sec | proj_peak_qps | avg_tokens_per_req | model_mix_large_pct | rec_headroom_pct | headroom_tokens/sec | reserved_gpu_slices | prewarm_start_min | prewarm_target_util_pct | fallback_model |
|-------------|--------------------------:|--------------:|-------------------:|--------------------:|-----------------:|--------------------:|--------------------:|------------------:|------------------------:|----------------|
| us-west-2   |                    420,000|         2,800 |                 150|                   42|                45|               189,000|                  9  |               8   |                     55 | gpt-medium-quant |
| us-east-1   |                    680,000|         4,533 |                 150|                   48|                40|               272,000|                 13  |              10   |                     60 | gpt-medium-quant |
| eu-west-1   |                    260,000|         1,733 |                 150|                   38|                50|               130,000|                  6  |               12  |                     50 | gpt-medium-quant |
| ap-southeast|                    140,000|           933 |                 150|                   36|                55|                77,000|                  4  |               18  |                     45 | gpt-small-quant  |

Notes on the table:
- proj_peak_tokens_per_sec: 99th percentile observed/forecasted short-window peak (10m rolling window) adjusted for growth patterns.
- rec_headroom_pct: recommended buffer above projected peak to absorb microbursts and GPU startup latency. Values tuned by region historical volatility and spot-interruption risk.
- reserved_gpu_slices: headroom_tokens/sec / 22,000 (rounded up). Example: us-east-1 -> 272k / 22k ≈ 12.4 => 13 slices.
- prewarm_start_min: minutes before predicted peak to bring slices online and warm KV caches. These are conservative for cross-region network variability.

HEADROOM SIZING RATIONALE & FORMULAS:
- headroom_tokens/sec = proj_peak_tokens_per_sec * (rec_headroom_pct / 100)
- reserved_gpu_slices = ceil(headroom_tokens/sec / tokens_per_gpu_slice)
- prewarm window length driven by: slice_friendly_boot_time + KV-warmup_time + safety_padding. Boot time baseline = 120s; KV warmup = variable (depends on recent cache hit rates).

SENSITIVITY SCENARIOS (quick checks):
1) +10% large-model share -> tokens/sec/latency cost impact: large models increase effective token cost per GPU by ~1.6x; headroom slices in us-east jump from 13 -> 16 under worst mix shift.
2) 2x short-window burst (10m) -> temporary additional 680k tokens/sec needed across region; immediate fallback triggers: route to lower-cost variants, extend prewarm, enable degraded sampling (reduce max tokens).
3) Region spot eviction event -> apply +15% safety multiplier to reserved slices and lengthen prewarm by +5m.

TAIL-LATENCY TRIGGERS (operational knobs):
- P99.9 > 1.6s for 3 consecutive minutes => auto-scale warm slices + 20% (up to reserved limit) and extend prewarm window by 2x.
- P99 > 750ms for 5 minutes => increase prewarm target util by -10pt (reduce target util to lower latency), and consider model fallback routing.

FALLBACK STRATEGY BY LOAD CLASS:
- Soft fallback: shift a fraction (10-25%) of new requests to quantized medium variants (gpt-medium-quant) when utilization > prewarm_target_util_pct for > 60s.
- Hard fallback: during sustained overload (>5m), route new heavy-generation requests to smaller models (gpt-small-quant) and enable brevity heuristics (max_tokens 0.6x).

OPERATIONAL PLAYBOOK (for Capacity & SRE):
1) Daily: regen 10m-rolling peak metrics per region, refresh reserved_gpu_slices if projection delta > 7%. Owner: Diego Martins.
2) Weekly: run model-mix sensitivity sweep (simulate +10% large) and publish delta to Product and Applied ML. Owner: Ava Chen.
3) Incident: If prewarm fails to recover P99 < SLA in 4 minutes, trigger cross-region routing per failover runbook INFRA-FF-07. Owner: on-call SRE.

METRICS TO PUBLISH TO CONSOLE (recommended):
- tokens/sec (1m/10m/1h) per region and per model-class.
- reserved_gpu_slices (allocated) vs used_slices (live).
- prewarm_start_time distribution and success rate.
- P99/P99.9 latencies mapped to target util pct.

OPEN QUESTIONS / DECISIONS NEEDED:
- Confirm tokens/sec per GPU-slice for L4-class hardware planned in APAC (action: capacity eval, Ravi Singh).
- Agree on a circuit-breaker threshold for automated fallback routing (default suggested: 80% of reserved headroom consumed for >90s).
- How to handle multi-tenant customers with isolated Dedicated pools that still need Hosted fallbacks? (product/legal input).

ACTION ITEMS (owner / due):
- Diego: wire up new daily DAG to compute rolling 10m peaks and publish to infra-metrics (due 2026-03-18).
- Ava: complete model-mix sensitivity report and upload to Confluence (due 2026-03-24).
- Ravi: run targeted perf runs to validate tokens/sec per GPU-slice for APAC hardware (due 2026-03-30).

APPENDIX: QUICK CALC GUIDE
- Example (us-west-2): proj_peak=420k tps, headroom=420k * 0.45 = 189k -> slices=ceil(189k / 22k)=9 -> recommended prewarm_start=8m (bring 9 slices online and warm KV).
- If P99.9 spikes during prewarm: reduce target util to 45% and add 2 extra slices as emergency buffer.

REVISION HISTORY:
- 2026-01-15: initial draft (Lena Patel).
- 2026-02-02: added fallback heuristics and sensitivity rows (Diego Martins).
- 2026-03-10: updated APAC prewarm windows after spot-interruption analysis (Ravi Singh).

END OF SHEET
